quarterly_data.signal: ArcelorMittal 6-K (H1 2026 interim report): sales $32,218 million, up 4.9% from $30,724 million; operating income $1,808 million (H1 2025: $2,757 million including a $1.9 billion Calvert bargain purchase gain); net income attributable to equity holders $1,258 million; steel shipments 26.2 million tonnes (27.4 million tonnes); average steel selling price $974 per tonne (+10.2%); iron ore production 26.4 million tonnes, Mining segment 19.8 million tonnes with ArcelorMittal Liberia at 7.7 million tonnes (+89.9%).
quarterly_data.figure: H1 2026 sales $32,218 million (+4.9%); shipments 26.2 million tonnes; $974 per tonne

quarterly_data.signal: ArcelorMittal 6-K: full-year 2026 capital expenditures are expected to remain within $4.5-$5.0 billion, of which $1.7-$1.9 billion for strategic growth projects; H1 2026 capex was $2.4 billion including a $0.2 billion MDA payment in Liberia; net interest expense is expected to be approximately $550 million in 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 capex $4.5-$5.0 billion; strategic growth $1.7-$1.9 billion; net interest approximately $550 million

quarterly_data.signal: ArcelorMittal 6-K (project updates): Mardyck electrical steels - first phase complete with the first commercial order delivered in Q2 2026, phase 2 now expected in the second half of 2027 and NOES volume revised to 155 thousand tonnes per year (previously 170 thousand tonnes); Gijon 1.1 million tonne EAF and Sestao capacity increase to 1.6 million tonnes expected in the second half of 2026; Dunkerque 2 million tonne EAF ramp-up in 2030 with Energy Efficiency Certificates support representing 50% of the EUR 1.3 billion investment; Serra Azul DRI pellet feed (approximately $0.5 billion) commissioned with the first vessel shipped in H1 2026; Liberia full completion expected in Q3 2026 and its railway being expanded to carry up to 30 million tonnes annually, reserved for ArcelorMittal, after a $200 million payment to the Government of Liberia for the mining-rights extension and reserved rail access.
quarterly_data.figure: NOES 155 thousand tonnes; Sestao 1.6 million tonnes; $200 million Liberia payment

quarterly_data.signal: ArcelorMittal 6-K (AMNS India): on March 23, 2026 AMNS India announced a greenfield integrated steel plant at Rajayyapeta, Andhra Pradesh, with Phase 1 capacity of 8.2 million tonnes per annum and Phase 1 capex of $7.5-$8.0 billion over five to six years, downstream capacity targeted for Q1 2029 and primary steelmaking for 2030/31, assuming remaining approvals including a long-term iron ore supply contract with NMDC; a detailed engineering study is under way to expand Hazira to 24 million tonnes; H1 2026 AMNS India sales (100% basis) were $3,275 million (+11.5%).
quarterly_data.figure: 8.2 million tonnes; $7.5-$8.0 billion; Hazira study to 24 million tonnes

quarterly_data.signal: ArcelorMittal 6-K (outlook): management expects European shipments in Q3 2026 to be stable to slightly higher than Q2, against a typical high-single-digit seasonal decline, and second-half 2026 shipments to exceed first-half shipments across all segments; it believes CBAM together with the TRQ trade tool from July 1, 2026 can support higher domestic capacity utilization and restore European profitability, and it names electrical steels a core growth focus with projects in the U.S. and Europe.

ArcelorMittal 6-K (portfolio): on May 18, 2026 it sold 23,869,984 Vallourec shares (10.4% of voting rights), retaining 18.0% and one board seat, with Vallourec remaining an equity-method associate; it recognized a $262 million impairment on its 25.2% stake in Baffinland Iron Mines, which is in financial difficulties and sought creditor protection; it completed the disposal of its Roman, Romania tubular facility on March 31, 2026 and classified its Costa Rica long-steel operations as held for sale.
quarterly_data.figure: Vallourec stake 18.0% after sale of 10.4%; $262 million Baffinland impairment

quarterly_data.signal: ArcelorMittal 6-K (legal proceedings): on January 29, 2026 it was served by the Extraordinary Commissioners of Acciaierie d'Italia (ADI) with a writ before the Court of Milan alleging mismanagement and value transfer from ADI to ArcelorMittal, seeking damages valued at EUR 7.0 billion (alternative valuation EUR 3.65 billion), which ArcelorMittal will defend vigorously; in June 2025 it started international arbitration against the Republic of Italy claiming damages in excess of EUR 1.8 billion; on May 15, 2026 ArcelorMittal Mining Canada settled two hundred Fisheries Act charges with Environment and Climate Change Canada for a payment of 70 (US$ millions), and in March 2026 it settled a Mexican tax assessment for a payment of 95.
quarterly_data.figure: EUR 7.0 billion claim; arbitration in excess of EUR 1.8 billion
